channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Financial Times] US floats unfreezing some Russian assets to restart Ukraine peace talks
item.description: European officials balked at proposal made by Donald Trump’s negotiators during meeting in Miami

item.title: [Politico Europe] Macron and Merz hold keys to an EU budget deal — but may be too weak to use them
item.description: The French and German leaders face political pressures that limit their room for maneuver on Europe's biggest negotiation.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Le Pen vows to downsize EU as she brings contribution cut fight to Brussels
item.description: The front-runner in France’s presidential reiterated her campaign promise to pare back payments to the EU by billions of euros ahead of a critical summit on Thursday.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s reliance on US gas is as serious a risk to EU and Ukrainian security as its addiction to Russian gas used to be
item.description: Europe's growing reliance on US gas imports is as serious a risk to EU and Ukrainian security as its historic addiction to Russian gas was.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs pause vote on EU pesticides bill, as UN experts join scientists in opposition to Big Pharma
item.description: Parliament’s environment and agriculture committees were originally expected to hold a joint vote on a compromise text on 5 October, but shelved that date without proposing another as this article went to publication.

item.title: [EU Observer] Black Sea becomes new front in Russia-Ukraine wars on grain exports, with no alternative EU route to get shipments out
item.description: New drone strikes on two ships in the Black Sea pose questions for the future of Russian and Ukrainian food exports to already struggling world markets.

item.title: [DW] Albania: Fire at Education Ministry as students protest
item.description: Riot police deployed in the Albanian capital Tirana on the second day of student protests. The sudden outbreak seemed at least somewhat reminiscent of the widespread demos in France courting international attention.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU bets on diplomacy, not blocking statute, to protect ICC from Trump sanctions
item.description: The EU has six months of diplomacy to reverse US-imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court, while shying away from triggering a rule that would protect Europeans.

item.title: [EU Observer] Musk joins Trump and Putin’s new axis of evil, as Starlink grounds Ukraine’s medium-range drones (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,693)
item.description: Ukrainian officers warn that Starlink’s sudden speed limits have grounded much of their drone fleet and weakened air defences, as massive Russian strikes leave millions facing blackouts.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU risks funding Israeli firms which help develop NAZA-type violent tech
item.description: Billions in EU research cash are already flowing to Israeli firms linked to drones, AI targeting and surveillance, raising questions over whether Europe is effectively bankrolling technologies used against Palestinian civilians.

item.title: [EU Observer] Leaders eye deep EU budget cuts, while long-term joint borrowing becomes the new normal
item.description: As leaders gather in Brussels, they must decide whether to keep pretending each new loan for Ukraine, defence, or other shocks is a one‑time exception, or finally admit that long‑term, risk‑managed joint borrowing has become the EU’s new normal.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU and Turkey explore closer trade ties to reduce dependence on China
item.description: The EU may not want Turkey as a member, but both sides can see the appeal of closer economic ties to reduce their dependencies on China.

item.title: [DW] Fact check: Misleading graph about alleged Russian bot activity
item.description: Did attacks on Russian data centers reduce bot activity around Germany's AfD? A viral graph claims they did. But it contains significant inconsistencies and provides no evidence to support the claim.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: When does a hybrid attack become an attack on Nato?
item.description: Two ships have been hit by drones in Bulgarian waters in the Black Sea on Monday. Several other ships have been targeted in recent weeks, at a time when Russia is intensifying its attacks on Ukraine.

item.title: [EU Observer] The ‘Transformative AI Strategy for Europe’ diagnoses the problem – but its solution is capitulation
item.description: Europe can only fully prepare for the AI transformation and maintain our sovereign control if the default action is to consider how can we use or create a European solution first, rather than capitulate to what Big Tech offers.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine allies in Poland after Starlink sabotage, Trump diesel deal
item.description: Germany's Johann Wadephul said hybrid plots like the Starlink fire showed Europe was "in Russia's crosshairs." The UK's Ed Miliband said Trump's Russian diesel deal led to a "very difficult few days" diplomatically.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine and the US: What's next after Trump's diesel deal with Russia?
item.description: Donald Trump plans to allow the purchase of Russian diesel, drawing criticism at home and abroad. What is behind the US president's decision and what should Ukraine do next? DW spoke with experts.

item.title: [EU Observer] Could Islamophobia one day become EU law?
item.description: An Islamophobic EU Parliament motion has showed that Europe's Muslims have reached an impossible crossroads - to integrate and forget their roots, or stay true to their traditions and risk being treated as a fifth column.

item.title: [EU Observer] Low pay and stress forcing Europe’s care workers to quit jobs, unions warn
item.description: Almost half of workers helping families care for children, older people, and people with disabilities in Europe have considered quitting due to low pay and bad working conditions.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukraine killing record number of Russian troops, as Putin resorts to using gangs to boost enlistment (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,692)
item.description: Soaring Russian casualty rates and shrinking recruitment mean frontline units risk running out of men to hold or advance in Donbas, even as Ukraine keeps blowing up their supply trucks and fuel tankers.

item.title: [DW] Critics warn of espionage risks as Slovakia restores military-diplomatic representation with Russia
item.description: Slovakia is restoring military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since 2022. The government has defended the move but critics warn of espionage risks and further damage to trust within NATO.

item.title: [DW] Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
item.description: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

item.title: [DW] What is holding back Cyprus's Schengen ambitions?
item.description: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Yet questions relating to the island's division and British military bases could still complicate its path to Europe's border-free travel zone.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Will Andy Burnham manage to bring the UK back into the EU?
item.description: Ten years after the Brexit vote, more and more Britons are asking whether they should go back. According to a YouGov poll conducted earlier this month, 52% would vote to rejoin the EU in a referendum.

item.title: [Financial Times] Chipmaker TSMC profits surge amid relentless AI demand
item.description: Taiwanese manufacturer beats estimates in third quarter with earnings of $23.6bn

item.title: [Politico Europe] The extremes of Reform: What will Farage do?
item.description: Is Reform facing another growing crisis over alleged racist, sexist and violent language within its ranks? Sam Coates and Anne McElvoy assess what the latest claims within an ITV News undercover investigation mean for Nigel Farage and whether more damaging revelations are still to come. Reform says there is “no room for racism” within the […]

item.title: [Financial Times] Global stocks sell-off deepens as chipmakers tumble
item.description: European and Asian equities slide as investors question durability of AI boom

item.title: [DW] EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget
item.description: EU leaders meeting in Brussels will examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. But they will also be looking to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of some major elections next year.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘He seemed happy’. Families still waiting for news of vanished Ceuta migrants, as EU leaders discuss stronger borders
item.description: Disappeared Moroccan migrants are likely "in the thousands" after a sudden wave of arrivals hit Ceuta. But despite the human tragedy, the EU leaders' main focus this week will be how to fortify borders.

item.title: [Financial Times] Ukraine to resume strikes on Russian refineries, Zelenskyy says
item.description: Ukrainian president expresses anger in FT interview at ‘dangerous’ withdrawal of US intelligence sharing and weakening of Starlink satellite internet service

item.title: [Financial Times] London’s gold market enjoys the Trump effect
item.description: The City’s dominance of physical trading in the metal is being reinforced by global instability

item.title: [Financial Times] Marsh to shoulder biggest chunk of Greensill settlement with Credit Suisse
item.description: Deal is rare example of broker bearing largest share of a settlement rather than insurers who wrote policies

item.title: [Financial Times] The man who would lead McKinsey
item.description: North America boss Eric Kutcher is the candidate to beat in the consultancy’s byzantine election

item.title: [Financial Times] Is the K-shaped economy really more of an E?
item.description: America remains a very unequal place, but on many metrics inequality is not increasing

item.title: [Financial Times] French debt worries spill into stocks, driving biggest underperformance since 2010
item.description: Investors demand big discounts against regional peers to reflect troubled public finances and looming presidential election

item.title: [Financial Times] Salmon producers start feeding chicken to fish
item.description: Fears of consumer backlash pushed aside as producers respond to surge in fishmeal prices

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU leaders face off over the budget
item.description: EU leaders meet today for their first chance to beef about the budget face to face. On the show, Zoya Sheftalovich and Sarah Wheaton dive deeper into why leaders look increasingly unlikely to reach an agreement on the EU’s next money pot by December. Plus, Zoya obtained a document revealing deepening relations between Russia and […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Das Rot-Grün-Rot-Dilemma in der Hauptstadt
item.description: Die Berliner Landespolitik manövriert sich erst in eine Sackgasse und will nun doch daraus rausfinden. Wegen des Streits um antisemitische Strömungen in der Linkspartei stehen die Sondierungsgespräche mit SPD und Grünen auf der Kippe, werden aber heute fortgesetzt. Wie sich das rot-grün-rote Bündnis gegen den Widerstand von SPD und Grünen im Bund retten will, zeigt […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK polling watchdog faces reckoning after Farage sting
item.description: British Polling Council members have pressed for tougher action on a firm accused of downplaying Reform UK links to its polling.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Frontex suspends reintegration program after blowing through its budget
item.description: The pause comes ahead of a proposed expansion of the EU border agency's role in returns, sharpening questions over how Brussels will fund its tougher deportation policy.

item.title: [Politico Europe] How Russia plans to revive its ties with Slovakia
item.description: With Viktor Orbán gone, Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico is emerging as Vladimir Putin’s most prominent ally in the EU.

item.title: [Politico Europe] How Putin’s favorite sport reopened the door to international contests
item.description: Brussels officials are grappling with the gradual reintegration of Moscow’s athletes, according to a document viewed by POLITICO.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Why Ukrainian strikes on data centers are a real problem for Russia — and beyond
item.description: Servers have become a target of war. As well as disrupting daily life, the strikes are raising questions of international law.

item.title: [Financial Times] Anthropic tells investors its quarterly revenue jumped 50%
item.description: Rapid growth is slower than some anticipated as fears about AI trade rattle markets

item.title: [DW] Who are the Ukrainian 'volunteers' under Russian command?
item.description: Russia has announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian "volunteers." But veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.

item.title: [DW] Trump claims Russia and Ukraine agreed to 'energy ceasefire'
item.description: US President Donald Trump says both sides have agreed to stop targeting oil refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure immediately.

item.title: [DW] Georgia's surrogacy industry is booming, but at what cost?
item.description: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.

item.title: [DW] UK: Iran 'highly likely' to be behind RAF Fairford incident
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. The government summoned Iran's ambassador. The scare at RAF Fairford led to the withdrawal of USAF B-1 heavy bombers.

item.title: [DW] Poland reports arrests of 2 Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with Starlink station fire last month
item.description: Polish authorities have reported the arrests of two Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with alleged sabotage of a Starlink station last month. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the fire an act of "hybrid warfare."

item.title: [DW] Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
item.description: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.

item.title: [DW] Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
item.description: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.
